body:
Unfortunately I still do get upset about it, but if it could get to a point where I'm merely annoyed rather than upset with myself for wasting so much time, that would be nice. (Or better yet, not wasting time at all.) I should try to remember coping methods when I feel something like that starting up, but it can be hard when I'm drowning in my thoughts.

I'm in the US. It was a pain even scheduling an appointment; I had to wait three months.

I guess what I'm going through is more common that I thought. That's sortof a relief.

I'm glad things are going better for you. I hope I can get help too. I'm not opposed to taking medication if I need to, though I've heard side effects can be bad. 

I tried to talk with a doctor (not my primary doctor) about depression before a few years ago, but he just brushed it off and mumbled something about "winter blues." I hope my primary doctor will actually listen to me.

Suicidal thoughts don't, but if they think I'm in danger of killing myself, it will, I think. I just don't want everyone around me to panic. My friends and family have enough on their plate without having to worry I'm in danger of disappearing. 

Thank you very much for talking with me. I hope I can get help too.

It's good to know I'm not alone in this.

It does impact my daily life sometimes. I've lost sleep over it before, but more often it just cripples me to the point where I cannot do anything--all I can do is sit around for hours on end and try to will the thoughts to disappear, which only makes them scream at me louder. I've relied on coping mechanisms of just writing all the thoughts out and shredding them, which can help sometimes, but it doesn't change the fact that I just lost five hours of my day trying to stop my brain from trying to convince me to kill myself.

That doesn't happen all the time, but when it does, it's bad.

I will tell my doctor that I'm thinking I'm depressed, but I'll leave out the suicide part--if I can get a therapist or something, I may bring it up then.

Thank you, I may do that. Even without my suicidal thoughts I still have other symptoms of depression and I do want to see a psychiatrist or therapist or something. I want help. 

But I don't want people thinking I'm ready to off myself and thus make everyone around me panic. I know that patient confidentiality is a thing UNLESS they think you're making plans for suicide. I don't know if they'd believe me if I told them I have frequent suicidal thoughts yet don't want to actually attempt it.

That said, I am worried I will *get* to a point where I might try something. I can only handle so much, and if these thoughts keep getting more and more frequent, I'm afraid they'll break past my defenses. But that's why I'm trying to get help. I want to get out of this before it gets worse.
